encounters.cc: Progressive joint pain and stiffness in knees and wrists with acute episodic swelling

lines: Progressive joint pain and stiffness in knees and wrists with acute episodic swelling
The patient is a 46-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis and established iron deposition arthropathy who returns for further evaluation of progressive joint symptoms.

Having been previously assessed in Gastroenterology and Internal Medicine for similar complaints, he presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of progressive joint pain and stiffness, particularly in his knees and wrists.
He also reports experiencing several episodes of acute knee pain with swelling, which resolved spontaneously over a few days.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2 years duration, secondary to hemochromatosis)
He has a history of type 2 diabetes and was recently diagnosed with cirrhosis during an evaluation for persistent fatigue and abdominal distension.
His family history is notable for similar joint problems in his father.
Alcohol: Former heavy alcohol use; abstinent for 3 years (history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission).
On physical examination, his liver is palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin, and there is mild tenderness over the affected joints without significant warmth or erythema.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue, lower extremity swelling, and early satiety with exertional dyspnea

lines: Progressive fatigue, lower extremity swelling, and early satiety with exertional dyspnea
Patient returns with hereditary hemochromatosis and arthropathy previously managed in gastroenterology, internal medicine, and rheumatology.
He presents with progressive fatigue, lower extremity swelling, and early satiety over the past 6 months.
He reports mild exertional dyspnea but denies chest pain.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2 years duration, secondary to hemochromatosis)
- Father: Hemochromatosis with cirrhosis and diabetes (deceased age 58)
Alcohol: Former heavy alcohol use; abstinent for 3 years (history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission).
Jugular venous distension, hepatomegaly, bilateral pitting edema, and clear lung fields.
There is darkening of the skin of the hands and forearms.
Cardiac auscultation reveals normal S1 and S2 with an S4 gallop.
Echocardiogram shows normal left ventricular size with marked concentric thickening of the ventricular walls and biatrial enlargement.
Left ventricular ejection fraction is preserved.

encounters.cc: Severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back after large meal

lines: Severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back after large meal

The patient is a 49-year-old male with a history of hereditary hemochromatosis complicated by arthropathy and restrictive cardiomyopathy who presents to the emergency department with 18 hours of severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back.
The pain began suddenly after a large dinner and has progressively worsened.
He has associated nausea and several episodes of nonbloody vomiting.
He denies alcohol use, gallstone history, recent trauma, or prior similar episodes.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2 years duration, secondary to hemochromatosis)
His medical history is notable for type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, and poorly controlled hyperlipidemia.
He does not take any medications regularly due to cost concerns.
He has no family history of pancreatic or gallbladder disease.
Alcohol: Former heavy alcohol use; abstinent for 3 years (history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission).
Temperature of 37.9°C (100.2°F), pulse 108/min, and blood pressure 138/84 mm Hg
On examination, he is in moderate distress.
Abdominal examination reveals epigastric tenderness without rebound or guarding.
Abdominal CT with contrast demonstrates an enlarged pancreas with peripancreatic fat stranding and no evidence of necrosis or pseudocyst formation.

lines: Nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain with metabolic decompensation

- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2 years duration, secondary to hemochromatosis)
- Father: Hemochromatosis with cirrhosis and diabetes (deceased age 58)
Alcohol: Former heavy alcohol use; abstinent for 3 years (history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission).
His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), blood pressure is 110/70 mmHg, pulse is 105/min, and respiratory rate is 28/min.
He appears lethargic and has deep, rapid breathing.

encounters.cc: Fever, chills, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to right shoulder

lines: Fever, chills, and right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to right shoulder
This 51-year-old male with hereditary hemochromatosis and cirrhosis presents with acute abdominal pain.
He reports that the pain is constant, sharp, and radiates to his right shoulder.
He also complains of nausea and decreased appetite.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2 years duration, secondary to hemochromatosis)
- Father: Hemochromatosis with cirrhosis and diabetes (deceased age 58)
Alcohol: Former heavy alcohol use; abstinent for 3 years (history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission).
His temperature is 38.9°C (102°F), heart rate is 110 beats per minute, and blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg
Abdominal examination reveals hepatomegaly and tenderness on palpation of the right upper quadrant.
Chest auscultation notes decreased breath sounds at the right base.
An abdominal ultrasound reveals a hypoechoic lesion in the right lobe of the liver.
There is also evidence of a small right-sided pleural effusion.

encounters.cc: Severe throbbing perianal pain intensifying with bowel movements and sitting

lines: Severe throbbing perianal pain intensifying with bowel movements and sitting
The patient with hemochromatosis, cirrhosis, and diabetes presents with perianal pain.
He reports the pain intensifies during bowel movements and while sitting.
He denies any recent trauma or sexual activity.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (2 years duration, secondary to hemochromatosis)
His diabetes is managed with metformin.
- Father: Hemochromatosis with cirrhosis and diabetes (deceased age 58)
Alcohol: Former heavy alcohol use; abstinent for 3 years (history of alcohol use disorder, in sustained remission).
On examination, the patient is febrile with a temperature of 38.5°C (101.3°F).
Inspection of the perianal area reveals erythema, edema, and a fluctuant mass near the anal verge.
Digital rectal examination is extremely painful and the patient is unable to tolerate it.
